title: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: Chapter Introduction
summary: Vanilla, cinnamon, vinegar and nail-polish remover share one secret: the carbonyl group, C=O. What sits on the carbonyl carbon makes an aldehyde, a ketone or a carboxylic acid, and what this chapter will cover.
keyPoints: Aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids all contain the **carbonyl group, C=O**.
**Aldehyde**: at least one **H** on the carbonyl carbon (R–CHO), e.g. vanillin, cinnamaldehyde.
**Ketone**: **two carbon groups** on it (R–CO–R′), e.g. acetone in nail-polish remover.
**Carboxylic acid**: an **–OH** on it (R–COOH), e.g. acetic acid in vinegar.

blocks.p: How these compounds are made; why the polar C=O undergoes **nucleophilic addition**; tests that tell an **aldehyde from a ketone**; and why carboxylic acids are **acidic**.

quiz.q: The group common to aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids is:
quiz.explain: All three contain the carbonyl group.

quiz.q: Acetone, the solvent in nail-polish remover, is:
quiz.explain: CH₃COCH₃ has two carbon groups on the carbonyl carbon.

quiz.q: Which has at least one H on the carbonyl carbon?

quiz.explain: Vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic (ethanoic) acid.

simulation.reason: A chapter introduction that names the carbonyl group and its three families; there is no quantity or process for a student to vary.
